title: Speech therapy
what: A specialist teaches correct sounds and develops speech and understanding. They work with both children and adults.
why: When a child says sounds poorly, started talking late, or talks little. For adults, after a stroke or injury, and for stuttering.
duration: a session usually lasts 30 to 45 minutes; the course usually runs several months
tell_doctor: At what age your child started talking and what worries you
How your child hears, and if hearing was tested
Any reports from a neurologist or ENT doctor
For adults: when speech changed, and after what

prepare.title: For parents
prepare.text: Write down what worries you about your child's speech. You can film a short video of how they talk at home.

prepare.title: Your child
prepare.text: Come when your child has slept well and is not hungry.

bring: Doctors' reports, if you have them
steps: The therapist gets to know you and asks about development
They look at how the lips and tongue move
Games, pictures, and tasks are offered
They note which sounds and skills need work
You get tasks to practice at home
feel: Nothing unpleasant. The session is like a game
Your child may be shy at the first session. That is normal
after: Do the home tasks a little every day
Praise effort, and do not correct your child harshly

faq.q: At what age should we see a speech therapist?
faq.a: If your child barely talks at 2, it is worth a visit. Sound correction usually starts at 4 to 5.

faq.q: Will it go away on its own?
faq.a: Sometimes, but it is better to ask a specialist. Starting early helps progress faster.

reminders.text: Speech therapy tomorrow. Bring the homework notebook and doctors' reports.
